   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> January 11, 2018, </em>the Parent Corporation issued $<ix:nonFraction id="c140474644" contextRef="i_2018-01-11_DebtInstrumentAxis-TheNotesMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-SubordinatedDebtMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">75</ix:nonFraction> million in aggregate principal amount of fixed-to-floating rate subordinated notes (the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2018</em> Notes&#8221;). The <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em> Notes bore interest at a rate that resets quarterly to an interest rate per annum equal to the then current <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>-month LIBOR rate plus <ix:nonFraction id="c140474648" contextRef="d_2018-01-11_2018-01-11_DebtInstrumentAxis-TheNotesMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-SubordinatedDebtMember_VariableRateAxis-LIBORLondonInterbankOfferedRateMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" scale="-4" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">284</ix:nonFraction> basis points (<ix:nonFraction id="c140474649" contextRef="d_2018-01-11_2018-01-11_DebtInstrumentAxis-TheNotesMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-SubordinatedDebtMember_VariableRateAxis-LIBORLondonInterbankOfferedRateMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">2.84</ix:nonFraction>%) payable quarterly in arrears.    <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><b></b><ix:exclude><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">11</em>&#160;</b>&#8211;<b> Income Taxes </b>&#8211;<b> (continued)</b></ix:exclude><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In assessing the realization of deferred tax assets, management considers whether it is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that some or all of the deferred tax assets will be realized. This assessment includes the evaluation of future taxable income, the scheduled reversal of deferred tax liabilities, and available tax planning strategies. In connection with the acquisition of FLIC, the Company obtained net operating loss carryforwards and other tax attributes that are subject to utilization limits under Internal Revenue Code Section <em style="font: inherit;">382.</em> These limits affect both realized and unrealized built-in losses and <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>restrict the Company's ability to utilize these attributes during the carryforward period. Accordingly, management established a valuation allowance against the relevant acquired deferred tax assets based on its evaluation of their future realizability. Refer to Note <em style="font: inherit;">2,</em> Business Combinations, for additional information regarding the FLIC acquisition. Aside from these acquired attributes, the Company believes its remaining net deferred tax assets are more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to be realized as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025&#160;</em>and as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024. </em>The Company has <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> unrecognized tax benefits as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024.&#160;</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company files income tax returns in multiple jurisdictions and is subject to examination by federal, state, and local taxing authorities. The Company regularly assesses developments in tax laws and regulations that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>impact its effective tax rate and financial reporting. The Company&#8217;s federal income tax returns that are currently open and subject to examination are from the tax year <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140474667">2022</span> return and forward. The Company&#8217;s state income tax returns are generally open from the tax year <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140474668">2021</span>&#160;and forward based on individual state statutes of limitations.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -4pt; text-indent: 36pt;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>the Company had state net operating loss carryforwards of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c140474669" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-StateAndLocalJurisdictionMember_IncomeTaxAuthorityNameAxis-NewJerseyDivisionOfTaxationMember" unitRef="USD" name="cnob:OperatingLossCarryforwardsSubjectToExpiration" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">134</ix:nonFraction> million, which expire at various dates from <em style="font: inherit;">2041</em> through <em style="font: inherit;">2045.</em>&#160;Additionally, the Company generated Recognized Built-In Losses (RBILs) of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140474672" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="cnob:TaxesRecognizedBuiltinLosses" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">26.5</ix:nonFraction> million which <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be carried forward indefinitely for federal tax purposes and expire in <em style="font: inherit;">2045</em>&#160;for the state tax purposes. The Company also had federal interest expense disallowance carryforwards of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c140474674" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="cnob:TaxCarryforwardsFederal162jCarryforwards" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">24.9</ix:nonFraction> million, which <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be carried forward indefinitely.&#160;These attributes are subject to utilization limits under Section <em style="font: inherit;">382,</em> which is $<ix:nonFraction id="c140474676" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="cnob:TaxUtilizationLimitsUnderSection382" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">9.7</ix:nonFraction> million. A valuation allowance has been established solely against certain state net operating loss and state RBIL carryforwards that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to be realized before expiration or utilization.</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:CommitmentsAndContingenciesDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3110435" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">13</em>&#160;</b>&#8211;<b> Commitments, Contingencies and Concentrations of Credit Risk</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">In the normal course of business, the Company has outstanding commitments and contingent liabilities, such as standby and commercial letters of credit, unused portions of lines of credit and commitments to extend various types of credit. Commitments to extend credit and standby letters of credit generally do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> exceed <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">These financial instruments involve, to varying degrees, elements of credit risk in excess of the amounts recognized in the consolidated financial statements. The commitment or contract amount of these financial instruments is an indicator of the Company&#8217;s level of involvement in each type of instrument as well as the exposure to credit loss in the event of nonperformance by the other party to the financial instrument.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company controls the credit risk of these financial instruments through credit approvals, limits and monitoring procedures. To minimize potential credit risk, the Company generally requires collateral and other credit-related terms and conditions from the client. In the opinion of management, the financial condition of the Company will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be materially affected by the final outcome of these commitments and contingent liabilities. A substantial portion of the Bank&#8217;s loans are secured by real estate located in New Jersey and New York. Accordingly, the collectability of a substantial portion of the loan portfolio of the Bank is susceptible to changes in the metropolitan New York real estate market.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The following table provides a summary of financial instruments with off-balance sheet risk as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:StockholdersEquityNoteDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3110439" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">15</em>&#160;</b>&#8211;<b> Stockholders</b>&#8217;<b> Equity and Regulatory Requirements</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Banks and bank holding companies are subject to regulatory capital requirements administered by federal banking agencies. Capital adequacy guidelines and, additionally for banks, prompt corrective action regulations, involve quantitative measures of assets, liabilities, and certain off-balance-sheet items calculated under regulatory accounting practices. Capital amounts and classifications are also subject to qualitative judgments by regulators. Failure to meet capital requirements can initiate regulatory action. The accumulated other comprehensive gain or loss on securities and derivatives is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> included&#160;in computing regulatory capital. Management believes as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the Bank and the Parent Corporation meet all capital adequacy requirements to which they are subject.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Prompt corrective action regulations provide <em style="font: inherit;">five</em> classifications: well-capitalized, adequately capitalized, undercapitalized, significantly undercapitalized and critically undercapitalized, although these terms are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> used to represent overall financial condition. If an institution is classified as adequately capitalized or lower, regulatory approval is required to accept brokered deposits. If undercapitalized, capital distributions are limited, as is growth and expansion, and capital restoration plans are required. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024,</em> the most recent regulatory notifications categorized the Bank as well capitalized under the regulatory framework for prompt corrective action. There are <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> conditions or events since that notification that management believes have changed the institution&#8217;s category.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">16</em>&#160;</b>&#8211;<b> Comprehensive Income</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Total comprehensive income includes all changes in equity during a period from transactions and other events and circumstances from non-owner sources. The Company&#8217;s other comprehensive income is comprised of unrealized holding gains and losses on securities available-for-sale, unrealized gains and losses on cash flow hedges, obligations for defined benefit pension plan and an adjustment to reflect the curtailment of the Company&#8217;s defined benefit pension plan, each net of taxes.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">17</em>&#160;</b>&#8211;<b>&#160;Pension and Other Benefits</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Defined Benefit Plans</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company maintains a frozen, noncontributory pension plan covering employees of the Company prior to the merger with Legacy ConnectOne (&#8220;Legacy CNOB Plan&#8221;). The benefits are based on years of service and the employee&#8217;s compensation over the prior <em style="font: inherit;">five</em>-year period. The plan&#8217;s benefits are payable in the form of a <em style="font: inherit;">ten</em>-year certain and life annuity. The plan is intended to be a tax-qualified defined benefit plan under Section <em style="font: inherit;">401</em>(a) of the Internal Revenue Code. Payments <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be made under the Pension Plan once attaining the normal retirement age of <em style="font: inherit;">65</em> and are generally equal to <em style="font: inherit;">44%</em> of a participant&#8217;s highest average compensation over a <em style="font: inherit;">5</em>-year period.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -36pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b><i>FLIC Merger</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In the FLIC merger, the Company acquired a defined benefit pension plan (&#8220;Legacy FLIC Plan&#8221; and, with the Legacy CNOB Plan, the &#8220;Plans&#8221;)) with a net funded status of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140474733" contextRef="i_2025-06-01_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanFundedStatusOfPlan" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">11.2</ix:nonFraction> million as of the Acquisition Date. Former FLIC employees were eligible to participate in the Pension Plan after attaining <ix:nonFraction id="c140474734" contextRef="i_2025-06-01_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="Pure" name="cnob:DefinedBenefitPlanMinimumAgeOfEmployee" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">21</ix:nonFraction> years of age and completing <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-06-01_2025-06-01_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" name="cnob:DefinedBenefitPlanMinimumService" id="c140474735" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">12</ix:nonNumeric> full months of service. Pension benefits are generally based on a percentage of average annual compensation during the period of creditable service. FLIC historically made&#160;contributions to the Pension Plan which, when taken together with participant contributions equal to <ix:nonFraction id="c140474736" contextRef="d_2025-06-01_2025-06-01_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="Pure" name="cnob:DefinedBenefitPlanEmployerMatchingContributionPercentOfEmployeesGrossPay" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">2</ix:nonFraction>% of their compensation, will be sufficient to fund these benefits. The Bank&#8217;s funding method, the unit credit actuarial cost method, is consistent with the funding requirements of applicable federal laws and regulations which set forth both minimum required and maximum tax-deductible contributions. Employees became fully vested after <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140474737">four</span> years&#160;of participation in the Pension Plan (<em style="font: inherit;">no</em> vesting occurs during the <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140474739">four</span>-year period). An internal management committee oversees the affairs of the pension plan and acts as named fiduciary.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Effective <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025, </em>the Company froze benefit accruals under the Legacy FLIC Plan&#160;for all participants. The freeze does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> affect retirees or vested benefits. The projected benefit obligation was remeasured using a discount rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c140474741" contextRef="i_2025-09-30_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanAssumptionsUsedCalculatingBenefitObligationDiscountRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">5.41</ix:nonFraction>%, increasing the liability by $<ix:nonFraction id="c140474742" contextRef="d_2025-09-30_2025-09-30_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanBenefitObligationPeriodIncreaseDecrease" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">2.0</ix:nonFraction> million. There were <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> other changes in assumptions. The freezing of the plan also resulted in the removal of projected salary increase from the liability determination, resulting in a curtailment gain of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140474744" contextRef="d_2025-07-01_2025-09-30_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanCurtailments" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5" sign="-">3.5</ix:nonFraction> million recognized in Noninterest income&#160;during the <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2025.</em> The plan&#8217;s funded status improved to <ix:nonFraction id="c140474747" contextRef="i_2025-09-30_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanFundedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">134</ix:nonFraction>%.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -5pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b>Significant Actuarial Assumptions. </b>The following tables set&#160;forth the significant actuarial assumptions used to determine the benefit obligation at the Acquisition Date:</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><b></b><ix:exclude><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">17</em></b>&#160;&#8211;<b> Pension and Other Benefits </b>&#8211;<b> (continued)</b></ix:exclude><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b>Plan Assets.&#160;</b>The objective for the Plans&#160;assets is to generate long-term investment returns from both income and capital appreciation which outpaces the rate of inflation, while maintaining sufficient liquidity to ensure the Plan&#8217;s ability to pay all anticipated benefit and expense obligations when due. The Plans <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>maintain a de minimis amount of cash equivalents, with the remaining assets allocated across <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> broadly-defined financial asset categories: (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>) equity, both domestic and international; and (<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>) fixed income of various durations and issuer type. The goal of the equity allocation is to supplement the Bank&#8217;s contributions to the Plans when the Plans are&#160;underfunded and increase surplus when the Plans are overfunded. The fixed income component will include longer-duration bonds designed to match and hedge the characteristics of the Plans&#8217; liabilities. Cash equivalents, under normal circumstances, will be temporary holdings for the purpose of paying expenses and monthly benefits.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">For fixed income investments: (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>) the minimum average credit quality shall be investment grade (Standard &amp; Poor&#8217;s BBB or Moody&#8217;s Baa) or higher; and (<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>) <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> more than <ix:nonFraction id="c140474756" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_CreditRatingMoodysAxis-MoodysBaa1RatingMember_DefinedBenefitPlanByPlanAssetCategoriesAxis-FixedIncomeFundsMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanPlanAssetsInvestmentWithinPlanAssetCategoryPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">5</ix:nonFraction>% of the portfolio <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be invested in securities with ratings below investment grade, and <em style="font: inherit;">none</em> <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be rated below investment grade at the time of purchase.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Reasonable precautions are taken to avoid excessive concentrations to protect the portfolio against unfavorable outcomes within an asset class. Specifically, the following guidelines are in place:</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;width:100%;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;"><tbody><tr><td style="vertical-align:top;width:auto;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:auto;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:auto;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">With the exception of fixed income investments explicitly guaranteed by the U.S. government, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> single investment security shall represent more than <ix:nonFraction id="c140474759" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_DefinedBenefitPlanByPlanAssetCategoriesAxis-SingleInvestmentSecurityExcludingFixedIncomeInvestmentsMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanPlanAssetsInvestmentWithinPlanAssetCategoryPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">5</ix:nonFraction>% of total Plan assets; and</p> </td></tr>
<tr><td style="vertical-align:top;width:auto;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:auto;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:auto;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">With the exception of passively managed investment vehicles seeking to match the returns of broadly diversified market indices or diversified investment vehicles chosen specifically to hedge the interest rate risk embedded in liabilities of the Plans, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> single investment pool or investment company (mutual fund) shall comprise more than <ix:nonFraction id="c140474761" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_DefinedBenefitPlanByPlanAssetCategoriesAxis-MutualFundMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanPlanAssetsInvestmentWithinPlanAssetCategoryPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">10</ix:nonFraction>% of total plan assets.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The portfolio will be rebalanced to the target asset allocation, if needed, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> less often than quarterly. Unless expressly authorized in writing by the Committee, the following investing activities are prohibited:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;width:100%;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;"><tbody><tr><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 1px;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 10.5028px;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 1571px;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Purchasing securities on margin;</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;width:100%;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;"><tbody><tr><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 1.49716px;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 9px;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 1572px;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Pledging or hypothecating securities, except for loans of securities that are fully collateralized;</p> </td></tr>

   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;width:100%;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;"><tbody><tr><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 1px;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 9px;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 1573px;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Purchasing or selling derivative securities for speculation or leverage; and</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;width:100%;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;"><tbody><tr><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 1.49716px;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 7px;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 1575px;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Engaging in investment strategies that have the potential to amplify or distort the risk of loss beyond a level that is reasonably expected given the objectives of the portfolio.</p> </td></tr>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The ranges for the weighted average expected long-term rates of return for equity funds, bond funds and total plan assets set forth in the preceding table represent an average of all expected allocation&#160;percentile returns. For these purposes, the trustee&#160;utilizes a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party&#160;capital markets model (the &#8220;model&#8221;), which&#160;forecasts distributions of future returns for a wide array of broad asset classes. The theoretical and empirical foundation of the model is that the returns of various asset classes reflect the compensation investors require for bearing different types of systematic risk. At the core of the model are estimates of the dynamic statistical relationship between risk factors and asset returns, obtained from statistical analysis based on available historical monthly financial and economic data.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The process of determining the overall expected long-term rate of return on plan assets begins with a review of appropriate investment data, including current yields on fixed income securities, historical investment data, historical plan performance and forecasts of inflation and future total returns for the various asset classes. This data forms the basis for the construction of a best-estimate range of real investment returns for each asset class. A weighted average real-return range is computed reflecting the Plans'&#160;expected asset mix, and that range, when combined with an expected inflation range, produces an overall best-estimate expected return range. Specific factors such as the Plans' investment policy, reinvestment risk and investment volatility are taken into consideration during the construction of the best estimate real return range, as well as in the selection of the final return assumption from within the range.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Plan Assets</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The general investment policy of the Pension Trust is for the fund to experience growth in assets that will allow the market value to exceed the value of benefit obligations over time. The Company&#8217;s pension plan asset allocation as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, target allocation, and expected long-term rate of return by asset are as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt;"><b><i>Fair Value of Plan Assets</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company used the following valuation methods and assumptions to estimate the fair value of assets held by the plan (for further information on fair value methods, see Note <em style="font: inherit;">21</em>):</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Equity securities and real estate funds</span>: The fair values for equity securities and real estate funds are determined by quoted market prices, if available (Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>). For securities where quoted prices are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> available, fair values are calculated based on market prices of similar securities (Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em>).</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b></b><ix:exclude><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">17</em>&#160;</b>&#8211;<b> Pension and Other Benefits </b>&#8211;<b> (continued)</b></ix:exclude><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Debt and fixed income securities</span>: Certain debt securities are valued at the closing price reported in the active market in which the bond is traded (Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>). Other debt securities are valued based upon recent bid prices or the average of recent bid and asked prices when available (Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em>) and, if <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> available, they are valued through matrix pricing models developed by sources considered by management to be reliable. Matrix pricing, which is a mathematical technique commonly used to price debt securities that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> actively traded, values debt securities without relying exclusively on quoted prices for the specific securities but rather by relying on the securities&#8217; relationship to other benchmark quoted securities (Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em>). For securities where quoted prices or market prices of similar securities are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> available, fair values are calculated using discounted cash flows or other market indicators (Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em>). Discounted cash flows are calculated using spread to continuous yield or quoted market pricing curves. During times when trading is more liquid, broker quotes are used (if available) to validate the model. Rating agency and industry research reports as well as defaults and deferrals on individual securities are reviewed and incorporated into the calculations.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The investment manager is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> authorized to purchase, acquire or otherwise hold certain types of market securities (subordinated bonds, real estate investment trusts, limited partnerships, naked puts, naked calls, stock index futures, oil, gas or mineral exploration ventures or unregistered securities) or to employ certain types of market techniques (margin purchases or short sales) or to mortgage, pledge, hypothecate, or in any manner transfer as security for indebtedness, any security owned or held by the Plan.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">18</em>&#160;</b>&#8211;<b> Stock Based Compensation</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company&#8217;s stockholders approved the <em style="font: inherit;">2017</em> Equity Compensation Plan (&#8220;the Plan&#8221;) on <em style="font: inherit;"> May 23, 2017. </em>The Plan eliminates all remaining issuable shares under previous plans and is the only outstanding plan as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025. </em>On <em style="font: inherit;"> May 30, 2023, </em>the Company's stockholders approved an amendment to the Plan that increased&#160;the maximum number&#160;of shares issuable to&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c140474829" contextRef="i_2017-05-23_PlanNameAxis-The2017EquityCompensationPlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,200,000</ix:nonFraction>. Grants under the Plan can be in the form of stock options (qualified or non-qualified), restricted shares, deferred stock&#160;units or performance units. Shares available for grant and issuance under the Plan as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> are approximately <ix:nonFraction id="c140474830" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_PlanNameAxis-The2017EquityCompensationPlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAvailableForGrant" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">169,899</ix:nonFraction>. The Company intends to issue all shares under the Plan in the form of newly issued shares.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">As of both <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025&#160;</em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024, </em>the Company did <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140474831"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140475279">not</span></span> have any outstanding stock options. Restricted stock and deferred stock units typically have a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140474832">three</span>-year vesting period starting <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year after the date of grant with <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140474834">one</span>-<em style="font: inherit;">third</em> vesting each year. Restricted stock granted to new employees and board members <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be granted with shorter vesting periods. Grants of performance units typically have a cliff vesting after <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140474836">three</span> years or upon a change of control. All issuances are subject to forfeiture if the recipient leaves or is terminated prior to the awards vesting. Restricted shares have the same dividend and voting rights as common stock, while options, performance units and deferred stock units do <em style="font: inherit;">not.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">All awards are issued at the fair value of the underlying shares at the grant date. The Company expenses the cost of the awards, which is determined to be the fair market value of the awards at the date of grant, ratably over the vesting period. Forfeiture rates are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> estimated but are recorded as incurred. Stock-based compensation expense was $<ix:nonFraction id="c140474839" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">4.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, $<ix:nonFraction id="c140474840" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">4.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140474841" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">4.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million for the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">2023,</em> respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Activity under the Company&#8217;s restricted shares for year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> was as follows:</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:DerivativeInstrumentsAndHedgingActivitiesDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3110471" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">20</em>&#160;</b>&#8211;<b> Derivatives</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">As part of our overall asset liability management and strategy the Company uses derivative instruments, which can include interest rate swaps, collars, caps, and floors.&#160;The notional amount does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> represent amounts exchanged by the parties.&#160;The amount exchanged is determined by reference to the notional amount and the other terms of the individual agreements. Derivative instruments are recognized on the balance sheet at their fair value and are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> reported on a net basis.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 16pt;"><b>Derivatives Designated as Hedges</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 16pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Subsequent changes in fair value for a hedging instrument that has been designated and qualifies as part of a hedging relationship are accounted for in the following manner:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 80pt;"><em style="font: inherit;">1</em>) Cash flow hedges: changes in fair value are recognized as a component in other comprehensive income</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 80pt;"><em style="font: inherit;">2</em>) Fair value hedges: changes in fair value are recognized concurrently in earnings</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 80pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">As long as a hedging instrument is designated and the results of the effectiveness testing support that the instrument qualifies for hedge accounting treatment, <em style="font: inherit;">100%</em> of the periodic changes in fair value of the hedging instrument are accounted for as outlined above. This is the case whether or <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> economic mismatches exist in the hedging relationship. As a result, there is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> periodic measurement or recognition of ineffectiveness. Rather, the full impact of hedge gains and losses is recognized in the period in which the hedged transactions impact earnings. The change in fair value of the hedging instrument that is included in the assessment of hedge effectiveness is presented in the same income statement line item that is used to present the earnings effect of the hedged item.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;"><b>&#160;Cash Flow Hedges</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company has&#160;entered into&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140474875">thirteen</span>&#160;pay fixed-rate interest rate swaps, with a total notional amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140474876" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-CommencedFixedInterestRateSwapsMember_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-CashFlowHedgingMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeLiabilityNotionalAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">700</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million.&#160;These are designated as cash flow hedges of outstanding&#160;Federal Home Loan Bank advances. We are required to pay fixed rates of interest ranging from <ix:nonFraction id="c140474877" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-CommencedFixedInterestRateSwapsMember_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-CashFlowHedgingMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DerivativeFixedInterestRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">0.63</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;to <ix:nonFraction id="c140474878" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-CommencedFixedInterestRateSwapsMember_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-CashFlowHedgingMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DerivativeFixedInterestRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">3.72</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;and receive variable rates of interest that reset quarterly based on the daily compounding secured overnight financing rate (&#8220;SOFR&#8221;).&#160;The swaps carry expiration dates ranging from&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 2026&#160;</em>to&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 2028.&#160;</em>The swaps are determined to be fully effective during the period presented and therefore&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;amount of ineffectiveness has been included in net income. Therefore, the aggregate fair value of the swap is recorded in other assets (liabilities) with changes in fair value recorded in other comprehensive income (loss). The amount included in accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) would be reclassified to current earnings should the hedges&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;longer be considered effective. The Company expects the hedges to remain fully effective during the remaining term of the swaps.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 7pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company previously entered into&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140474881">two</span>&#160;forward starting interest rate cap spread transactions,&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">one</em>&#160;with a total notional amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140474883" contextRef="i_2022-10-01_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateCapMember_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-CashFlowHedgingMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeLiabilityNotionalAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">150</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, which became&#160;effective on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> October 1, 2022&#160;</em>and which matures in&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> October&#160;</em>of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2027</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">one</em>&#160;interest rate cap spread transaction, with a total notional amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140474886" contextRef="i_2022-11-30_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateCapMember_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-CashFlowHedgingMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeLiabilityNotionalAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">75</ix:nonFraction> million, which became effective in&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 2022&#160;</em>and which matures in&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November&#160;</em>of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2027.</em>&#160;These are designated as cash flow hedges of brokered certificates of deposit, and the interest rate cap spread is indexed to a benchmark of fed funds with payment required&#160;on a monthly basis. The structure of these instruments is such that the Company entered into a total of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c140474888" contextRef="i_2022-12-31_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateCapMember_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-CashFlowHedgingMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember_PositionAxis-ShortMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeLiabilityNotionalAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">225</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million in notional amount of sold interest rate cap agreements, in which we are required to pay the counterparty an incremental amount if the index rate exceeds a set cap rate. Simultaneously, the Company purchased a total of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140474889" contextRef="i_2022-12-31_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateCapMember_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-CashFlowHedgingMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember_PositionAxis-LongMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeLiabilityNotionalAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">225</ix:nonFraction> million notional amount of interest rate cap agreements in which we receive an incremental amount if the index rate is above a set cap rate.&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">No</em>&#160;payments are required if the index rate is&#160;at, or below, the cap rate on the sold or purchased interest rate cap agreements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Interest income recorded on these swap and cap transactions totaled approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c140474891" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-CashFlowHedgingMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestIncomeExpenseNet" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">17.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, $<ix:nonFraction id="c140474892" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-CashFlowHedgingMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestIncomeExpenseNet" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">21.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140474893" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-CashFlowHedgingMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestIncomeExpenseNet" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">20.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million during <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2024,</em> and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>&#160;and is reported as a component of either interest expense on FHLB advances or&#160;brokered certificates of deposits.</p>

   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 7pt;"><b>&#160;Derivatives</b>&#160;<b><em style="font: inherit;">Not</em> Designated as Hedges</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 7pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">As part of the merger with FLIC, the Bank acquired interest rate swap agreements (each, a &#8220;back-to-back swap&#8221;) that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> designated as hedging instruments. A&#160;back-to-back swap allows a&#160;borrower to effectively convert a variable rate loan to a fixed rate. The Bank originates a variable rate loan with a borrower and simultaneously enters&#160;into offsetting back-to-back swaps&#160;with the borrower and an unaffiliated dealer counterparty to minimize interest rate risk. In connection with each swap transaction, the Bank agrees to pay interest to the borrower on a notional amount at a variable interest rate and receives interest from the borrower on a similar notional amount at a fixed interest rate. Concurrently, the Bank agrees to pay the dealer counterparty the same fixed interest rate on the same notional amount and receives the same variable interest rate on the same notional amount. Because the Bank acts as an intermediary for its borrower, changes in the fair value of the underlying derivative contracts offset each other and do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> impact the Bank&#8217;s results of operations.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 7pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The following table reflects the back-to-back swaps that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> designated as hedging instruments as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">31,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2025:</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 7pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock" id="c3110476" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">21</em>&#160;</b>&#8211;<b> Fair Value Measurements and Fair Value of Financial Instruments</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Fair value is the exchange price that would be received for an asset or paid to transfer a liability (exit price) in the principal or most advantageous market for the asset or liability in an orderly transaction between market participants on the measurement date.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">FASB ASC <em style="font: inherit;">820</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10,</em> &#8220;Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures&#8221;, is the standard used to govern disclosures related to fair value measurements.&#160;FASB ASC <em style="font: inherit;">820</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">05</em> defines fair value, establishes a framework for measuring fair value, establishes a <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>-level valuation hierarchy for disclosure of fair value measurements and enhances disclosure requirements for fair value measurements. The valuation hierarchy is based upon the transparency of inputs to the valuation of an asset or liability as of the measurement date.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">FASB ASC <em style="font: inherit;">820</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">65</em> provides additional guidance for estimating fair value in accordance with FASB ASC <em style="font: inherit;">820</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">05</em> when the volume and level of activity for the asset or liability have significantly decreased. This ASC also includes guidance on identifying circumstances that indicate a transaction is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> orderly.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">FASB ASC <em style="font: inherit;">820</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">05</em> establishes a fair value hierarchy that prioritizes the inputs to valuation methods used to measure fair value. The hierarchy gives the highest priority to unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities (Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> measurements) and the lowest priority to unobservable inputs (Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> measurements). The <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> levels of the fair value hierarchy under FASB ASC <em style="font: inherit;">820</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">05</em> are as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><i>Level <em style="font: inherit;">1:</em></i> Unadjusted quoted prices in active markets that are accessible at the measurement date for identical, unrestricted assets or liabilities.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><i>Level <em style="font: inherit;">2:</em></i> Quoted prices for similar assets and liabilities in active markets, and inputs that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly, for substantially the full term of the financial instrument.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><i>Level <em style="font: inherit;">3:</em></i> Prices or valuation techniques that require inputs that are both significant to the fair value measurement and unobservable (for example, supported with little or <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> market activity).</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">An asset&#8217;s or liability&#8217;s level within the fair value hierarchy is based on the lowest level of input that is significant to the fair value measurement. The following information should <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be interpreted as an estimate of the fair value of the entire Company since a fair value calculation is only provided for a limited portion of the Company&#8217;s assets and liabilities. Due to the&#160;wide range of valuation techniques and the degree of subjectivity used in making the estimates, comparisons between the Company&#8217;s disclosures and those of other companies <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be meaningful.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

      </div>
     </div>
     <div class="hf-row">
      <div class="hf-cell" style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: center; font-weight: bold; margin: 0pt; width: 99.9%; display: inline-block;">

   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><b></b><ix:exclude><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">21</em>&#160;</b>&#8211;<b> Fair Value Measurements and Fair Value of Financial Instruments&#160;(continued)</b></ix:exclude><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b>Assets and Liabilities Measured at Fair Value on a Recurring Basis</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The following methods and assumptions were used to estimate the fair values of the Company&#8217;s assets measured at fair value on a recurring basis as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b><i>Securities Available-for-Sale:</i></b> Where quoted prices are available in an active market, securities are classified within Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> of the valuation hierarchy. Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> inputs include securities that have quoted prices in active markets for identical assets. If quoted market prices are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> available, then fair values are estimated by using pricing models, quoted prices of securities with similar characteristics, or discounted cash flows. Examples of instruments&#160;which would generally be classified within Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> of the valuation hierarchy include municipal bonds and certain agency collateralized mortgage obligations. In certain cases where there is limited activity in the market for a particular instrument, assumptions must be made to determine the fair value of the instruments, and these are classified as Level <em style="font: inherit;">3.</em> When measuring fair value, the valuation techniques available under the market approach, income approach and/or cost approach are used. The Company&#8217;s evaluations are based on market data and the Company employs combinations of these approaches for its valuation methods depending on the asset class.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b><i>Derivatives:</i></b> The fair value of derivatives is&#160;based on valuation models using observable market data as of the measurement date (level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em>). Our derivatives are traded in an over-the-counter market where quoted market prices are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> always available. Therefore, the fair values of derivatives are determined using quantitative models that utilize multiple market inputs. The inputs will vary based on the type of derivative, but could include interest rates, prices and indices to generate continuous yield or pricing curves, prepayment rate, and volatility factors to value the position. The majority of market inputs are actively quoted and can be validated through external sources, including brokers, market transactions and <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party pricing services.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Collateral Dependent Loans</span>: The Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>record adjustments to the carrying value of loans based on fair value measurements, either as an individually evaluated allowance or as partial charge-offs of the uncollectible portions of these loans. Individually evaluated allowances are calculated in accordance with GAAP. Individually evaluated allowances are generally based on the fair value of the underlying collateral supporting the loan and, as a result, the carrying value of the loan less the individually evaluated allowance amount applicable to that loan does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> necessarily represent the fair value of the loan. Real estate collateral is valued using independent appraisals or other indications of value based on recent comparable sales of similar properties or assumptions generally observable by market participants. However, due to the substantial judgment applied and limited volume of activity as compared to other assets, fair value is based on Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> inputs. Estimates of fair value used for collateral supporting commercial loans generally are based on assumptions <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> observable in the marketplace and are also based on Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> inputs.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b></b><ix:exclude><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">21</em>&#160;</b>&#8211;<b> Fair Value Measurements and Fair Value of Financial Instruments </b>&#8211;<b> (continued)</b></ix:exclude><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b>Fair Value of Financial Instruments</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">FASB ASC <em style="font: inherit;">825</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10</em> requires all entities to disclose the estimated fair value of their financial instrument assets and liabilities. For the Company, as for most financial institutions, the majority of its assets and liabilities are considered financial instruments as defined in FASB ASC <em style="font: inherit;">825</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10.</em> Many of the Company&#8217;s financial instruments, however, lack an available trading market as characterized by a willing buyer and willing seller engaging in an exchange transaction. It is also the Company&#8217;s general practice and intent to hold its financial instruments to maturity and <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to engage in trading or sales activities except for loans held-for-sale and investment securities available-for-sale. Therefore, significant estimations and assumptions, as well as present value calculations, were used by the Company for the purposes of this disclosure.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Fair values for financial instruments must be estimated by management using techniques such as discounted cash flow analysis and comparison to similar instruments. These estimates are highly subjective and require judgments regarding significant matters, such as the amount and timing of future cash flows and the selection of discount rates that appropriately reflect market and credit risks. Changes in these judgments often have a material effect on the fair value estimates. Since these estimates are made as of a specific point in time, they are susceptible to material near-term changes. Fair values disclosed in accordance with ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">825</em> do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> reflect any premium or discount that could result from the sale of a large volume of a particular financial instrument, nor do they reflect possible tax ramifications or estimated transaction costs.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b>Cash and cash equivalents.</b> The carrying amounts of cash and short-term instruments approximate fair values.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b>FHLB stock.</b> It is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> practical to determine the fair value of FHLB stock due to restrictions placed on its transferability.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b>Loans.</b> The fair value of portfolio loans, net is determined using an exit price methodology. The exit price methodology continues to be based on a discounted cash flow analysis, in which projected cash flows are based on contractual cash flows adjusted for prepayments for certain loan types (<i>e.g., </i>residential mortgage loans and multifamily loans) and the use of a discount rate based on expected relative risk of the cash flows. The discount rate selected considers loan type, maturity date, a liquidity premium, cost to service, and cost of capital, which is a Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> fair value estimate.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b>Deposits. </b>The carrying amounts of deposits with <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> stated maturities (i.e., noninterest-bearing, savings, NOW, and money market deposits) are assigned fair values equal to the carrying amounts payable on demand. The fair value of time deposits is based on the discounted value of contractual cash flows using estimated rates currently offered for alternative funding sources of similar remaining maturity.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b>Term Borrowings and Subordinated Debentures</b>. The fair value of the Company&#8217;s long-term borrowings and subordinated debentures were calculated using a discounted cash flow approach and applying discount rates currently offered based on weighted remaining maturities.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b>Accrued Interest Receivable/Payable. </b>The carrying amounts of accrued interest approximate fair value resulting in a Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> or Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> classification based on the level of the asset or liability with which the accrual is associated.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

      <div class="hf-cell" style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: center; font-weight: bold; margin: 0pt; width: 99.9%; display: inline-block;">
        CONNECTONE BANCORP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
      </div>
     </div>
     <div class="hf-row">
      <div class="hf-cell" style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: center; font-weight: bold; margin: 0pt; width: 99.9%; display: inline-block;">
        NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
      </div>
     </div>
    </div>
   </ix:exclude>
   <ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b></b><ix:exclude><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">21</em>&#160;</b>&#8211;<b> Fair Value Measurements and Fair Value of Financial Instruments </b>&#8211;<b> (continued)</b></ix:exclude><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The fair value of commitments to originate loans is estimated using the fees currently charged to enter into similar agreements, considering the remaining terms of the agreements and the present creditworthiness of the counterparties. For fixed-rate loan commitments, fair value also considers the difference between current levels of interest rates and the committed rates. The fair values of letters of credit and lines of credit are based on fees currently charged for similar agreements or on the estimated cost to terminate or otherwise settle the obligations with the counterparties at the reporting date. The fair value of commitments to originate loans is immaterial and <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> included in the tables above.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Changes in assumptions or estimation methodologies <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>have a material effect on these estimated fair values.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company&#8217;s remaining assets and liabilities, which are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> considered financial instruments, have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> been valued differently than has been customary with historical cost accounting. <em style="font: inherit;">No</em> disclosure of the relationship value of the Company&#8217;s core deposit base is required by FASB ASC <em style="font: inherit;">825</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Fair value estimates are based on existing balance sheet financial instruments, without attempting to estimate the value of anticipated future business and the value of assets and liabilities that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> considered financial instruments. For example, there are certain significant assets and liabilities that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> considered financial assets or liabilities, such as the brokerage network, deferred taxes, premises and equipment, and goodwill. In addition, the tax ramifications related to the realization of the unrealized gains and losses can have a significant effect on fair value estimates and have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> been considered in the estimates.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Management believes that reasonable comparability between financial institutions <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be likely, due to the wide range of permitted valuation techniques and numerous estimates which must be made, given the absence of active secondary markets for many of the financial instruments. This lack of uniform valuation methodologies also introduces a greater degree of subjectivity to these estimated fair values.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
